Bug_Title: Regex boundaries should not be used in a way that can never be matched
Bug_Details:
In regular expressions the boundaries ^ and \A can only match at the beginning of the input (or, in case of ^ in combination with the MULTILINE flag, the beginning of the line) and $ , \Z and \z only at the end.
These patterns can be misused, by accidentally switching ^ and $ for example, to create a pattern that can never
match.
Noncompliant code example
// This can never match because $ and ^ have been switched around
Pattern.compile("$[a-z]+^"); // Noncompliant
Compliant solution
Pattern.compile("^[a-z]+$");
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by using a regex pattern '$[a-z]+^' which can never match because the boundaries $ and ^ have been switched around. This pattern requires the string to end with a lowercase letter followed by the start of the string, which is logically impossible.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test cases call the showBug method with different inputs, all of which should return 'No match found' due to the invalid regex pattern '$[a-z]+^'. The test cases fail because they expect a match, which is logically impossible with the given pattern.
